video_title: Matas and Lonzo reunite - Ball in the Family Ep. 27

quotes.speaker: Matas Buzelis
quotes.summary_phrase: Matas Buzelis on the business side of the NBA
quotes.excerpt: I found out about the business side of basketball. It's a lot different.
quotes.quote: I found out about the business side of basketball. It's a lot different. We have a whole new team. Who stayed? Josh, Pat, and Sticks. That's it. That's the NBA, though. It's going to be moving, bro. I couldn't believe it, bro. Even the front office guys changed. It's completely new team, but I think it's exciting, a new chapter, and try to get it rolling.

quotes.speaker: Lonzo Ball
quotes.summary_phrase: Lonzo Ball on Matas Buzelis's role with the Bulls
quotes.excerpt: Matas is supposed to be here and lead the future of this team.
quotes.quote: The fact you're there is like, you're one of the guys. So that's there, your team for real. I got a lot to prove, though. I got a lot to prove. Always. You still doing the touch? Actually, I gave it up. Me and Pete got a new routine, so we've been working with Dirk a little bit.

quotes.speaker: Lonzo Ball
quotes.summary_phrase: Lonzo Ball on Matas Buzelis's potential
quotes.excerpt: Matas is a high pick. Matas is supposed to be here and lead the future of this team.
quotes.quote: My guy game. Matas is a high pick. Matas is supposed to be here and lead the future of this team. Bro shoots a step-back easy middy that he can probably make eight out of 10 times. He happens to miss it. By the way, just a casual miss. Wasn't an airball or nothing crazy or nothing. Billy stops the film, goes in, and said, take that shit and throw it in the garbage. I'm dying next to him. People are like, yo, what?

quotes.speaker: Lonzo Ball
quotes.summary_phrase: Lonzo Ball on Billy Donovan's coaching style
quotes.excerpt: It was very similar to when they told Julius Randle on the Lakers to just screen and rebound.
quotes.quote: It was very similar to when they told Julius Randle on the Lakers to just screen and rebound and don't do nothing else. I'm like, bro, we're in the NBA. These are like real players and you're putting them in a box. I feel like that's just not, it's not good for your mental. I respect Billy so much, though, because he's a straight shooter. Everything he says, it's either for the betterment of the team or to help you. And you have to respect a coach like that.

quotes.speaker: Matas Buzelis
quotes.summary_phrase: Matas Buzelis on the importance of routine
quotes.excerpt: The routine matters so much. I'd watch Kobe. It's the same thing every time.
quotes.quote: The routine matters so much. What they did, it's the same thing every time. I'd watch Kobe. It's the same thing every time. He'd literally take his clothes off the same, socks, shoe, shoe, same thing every time. Nothing different. Shoot the same time, eat the same time, take a piss the same time. I'm not even trolling. Everything is the same. That's what I started to do. You see, I hit my head on the backboard every time before the game. I do the same thing.

quotes.speaker: Matas Buzelis
quotes.summary_phrase: Matas Buzelis on wanting to work with Danny Avdija
quotes.excerpt: I feel like I was shooting too many threes. I need to get to the rim more.
quotes.quote: To be honest, who I really want to work with is Danny Avdija. I've been talking with him. It's just, I feel like I was shooting too many threes. I need to get to the rim more. I want to know like how he lowers his shoulder, how he attacks. I seen him in Vegas. We're supposed to work out this weekend. He's somebody, Franz Wagner, probably him, KD, of course. That's who everybody needs to work out with, but I think right now Danny Avdija.

quotes.speaker: Matas Buzelis
quotes.summary_phrase: Matas Buzelis on Chicago basketball culture
quotes.excerpt: It's like a junkyard dog. That's what I describe like a Chicago hooper is.
quotes.quote: It's like a junkyard dog. That's what I describe like a Chicago hooper is. It's those 5'11, 6-foot guards that are just so annoying to play against. I think that's why I also got like my handles at 6'10, is playing against those type of guys. They always pushed me in game and that's how I got, that's how I got better.

quotes.speaker: Matas Buzelis
quotes.summary_phrase: Matas Buzelis on his decision to play in the G League
quotes.excerpt: I knew I was going to the G League since I was 15.
quotes.quote: I hate how people were like, Matas went to the G League because of the money. People were making 2 million in college. I got offered some money to go to college, but it was never about the money. I couldn't really be in the college environment, to be honest. I knew I was going to the G League since I was 15. My coach kept telling me like, you going to Ignite, you going to Ignite. And it came to fruition.

quotes.speaker: Matas Buzelis
quotes.summary_phrase: Matas Buzelis on the intensity of the G League
quotes.excerpt: G League was tough because everyone's trying to prove something.
quotes.quote: G League was tough because everyone's trying to prove something. NBA is an opportunity league for most guys. Some people don't have that shot and they get put down there. They're not really supposed to be down there. You have a bunch of guys that are playing on TV every night. So those, the guys that come in aren't playing on TV. They're trying to get an NBA contract. So they come in and they're trying to just kill you. They don't care, they'll follow you, they'll hurt you.

quotes.speaker: Matas Buzelis
quotes.excerpt: Control what you can control. That's how you lose your mindset worrying about things you can't control.
quotes.quote: Control what you can control. That's how you lose your mindset worrying about things you can't control. I didn't play in the beginning of my career, so I know for a fact I can get up every morning and put a smile on my face and go to work. That's all I can do. And if the coach don't put me in that game, it's so be it, but I'm going to keep, I'm going to keep grinding, I'm going to keep getting better.
